title: The First Hike Since 2023
subtitle: RBI MPC 5–7 October 2026: a labelled composite CFO must decide whether to pre-empt a 25 bps repo move before the statement lands
description: HBS-style teaching case set four days before the RBI Monetary Policy Committee meeting of 5–7 October 2026. Public polls (Reuters 18–28 September; Moneycontrol 25 September) show a majority expecting the first 25 basis-point repo hike since February 2023, from 5.25% to 5.50%, after August CPI printed 4.82%. A composite listed manufacturer must choose among locking floating-rate lines now, waiting for the statement, or rewriting FY27 interest and guidance before the street does.
sources: Reuters (28 September 2026). RBI to raise interest rates to 5.50% in October as inflation broadens: Reuters poll. 35 of 61 economists expected +25 bps at the 5–7 October meeting.
Economic Times / PTI (29–30 September 2026). Coverage of the Reuters poll and Nomura note expecting October and December hikes toward 5.75%.
Moneycontrol (25 September 2026). MPC poll of 13 economists and treasury heads: majority expect repo at 5.50%; FY27 growth forecast retained at 6.7%.
RBI (August 2026). MPC held repo at 5.25%; upgraded FY27 GDP growth to 6.7%. Minutes noted several members, including Governor Sanjay Malhotra, would favour a hike if inflation broadened.
RBI / MOSPI public series. August 2026 CPI reported at 4.82%, above the 4% medium-term target for a third consecutive month (as cited in Reuters, 28 September 2026).
Federal Reserve (September 2026). 25 bps increase in the federal funds target range to 3.75–4.00%, as reported in Moneycontrol poll context.
